prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you have referred to the Fourth of July as 'the holidays.' Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, Members of the Committee,

I stand before you today to address this grave allegation with the solemnity it deserves. I wish to state for the record, clearly and unequivocally, that I have never referred to the Fourth of July as "the holidays."

To characterize our nation’s Independence Day with such a casual, pluralized, and commercially generic term would be an affront to the singular and sacred nature of the occasion. The Fourth of July is not merely a holiday among many; it is *the* anniversary of our founding, the birthday of American liberty, and a solemn remembrance of the sacrifices made to secure the blessings we enjoy today. To reduce it to "the holidays" would be to strip it of its unique historical weight and patriotic significance.

If I have been misheard or misquoted, I welcome the opportunity to set the record straight. My devotion to this nation and its founding principles is unwavering, and my language has always reflected the profound respect I hold for the Day of Independence. I have never used, nor would I ever use, terminology that diminishes the singular importance of July 4th.

I thank the Committee for allowing me to clarify this matter, and I remain ready to answer any further questions you may have.
